title: SSE resume & reassembly strategy for multiplexed response streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a robust SSE-based streaming layer that supports resumable connections, client-visible resume tokens, and safe reassembly for multiplexed logical streams (response, tool-calls, structured events). Goal: reduce visible duplication/corruption on reconnects, enable older clients to interoperate via a compatibility header, and provide deterministic semantics for structured chunks used by function/tool calling.
acceptance_criteria: Server sends event stream with deterministic per-chunk metadata: stream_id, seq_no, chunk_type, resume_token (opaque) and payload
On client reconnect with resume_token, server can resume from the next unacknowledged seq_no for that stream_id without duplicating side effects (idempotency semantics documented)
Support multiplexing at the protocol level so a single TCP/SSE connection can carry 'response', 'tool', and 'meta' logical streams and clients can opt into a subset
Legacy clients (no resume header) receive identical message ordering and graceful end-of-stream markers; compatibility switch via X-Redwood-Stream-Version header
Automated tests validate reassembly across chunk boundaries where a logical JSON object is split across multiple SSE events
Metrics for resumed connections, resumed-bytes, duplicate-chunks, and reassembly-failures are emitted and visible in console dashboards
technical_notes: Event format: text/event-stream events with 'event: chunk' and data equal to a single-line base64-encoded JSON blob to avoid event-stream newline issues

Chunk JSON fields: {"stream_id":string, "seq_no":int, "chunk_type":string, "final":bool, "resume_token":string|null, "payload":string} — payload is either base64-encoded binary or escaped JSON string depending on chunk_type
Resume token is opaque to client; server generates tokens per connection snapshot keyed by stream_id and seq_no. Tokens contain proof of position and short-lived signature to prevent reuse beyond TTL

Multiplexing: streams are independent logical queues. Reconnect semantics: client supplies last-seen resume_token per stream_id. Server validates and resumes only streams covered by token; others start from head or an explicit 'start_at' claim

Idempotency: tool/function calls must include a client-supplied idempotency_key in the payload (sdk will auto-generate). If a chunk that caused a side-effect is re-sent due to reconnect, server deduplicates by idempotency_key
Backpressure: server maintains per-stream in-flight window. If client reads slowly, server stalls or checkpoints resume_token to allow safe reconnection; customers can configure checkpoint frequency
Compatibility header: X-Redwood-Stream-Version: 2 enables multiplex/resume. Version 1 remains simple line-delimited SSE JSON without resume metadata for older SDKs
Security: resume tokens tied to auth session; tokens are short-lived (default 30s) and can be revoked when sessions rotate. Tokens are signed using KMS-derived key to prevent forgery
design_decisions: Use base64-encoded JSON in the SSE 'data' field to avoid multi-line event-parsing edge cases and to carry binary deltas for tokenizer-efficient updates
Keep resume token semantics opaque rather than sequence-only integers to allow the server to include routing/replica hints for continued correctness during leader failover
Multiplexing chosen over separate connections to reduce mobile/edge connection count and to simplify TLS/session management for high-cardinality customers
Require client idempotency_key for any chunk that can trigger external effects (e.g., tool invocation) to keep server-side dedupe simple and performant
Expose an opt-in compatibility header to avoid breaking existing SDKs while allowing gradual rollout
rollout_plan: Phase A (Canary 5%): server-level flag 'enable_mux_resume_v2' off by default. Enable for internal clients and early partners. Monitor resumed_conns and duplicate_events metrics
Phase B (50%): expand to public beta for new signups and SDK v2.0. Add console dashboard card for resumed connections and reassembly failures
Phase C (GA): enable by default for new regions. Provide migration guide for SDK v1 users including compatibility header samples and recommended timeouts
Fallback: if resume validation fails on reconnect, server returns 'event: stream_reset' with reason; client should reopen full stream and request full state snapshot via non-streaming API
test_plan: Unit tests for encoder/decoder: verify base64 roundtrip and multi-event JSON reassembly
Integration tests simulating flaky networks: drop mid-chunk, reconnect with resume_token, assert no duplicated side-effects (tool calls) when idempotency_key present
Load tests: measure CPU/memory overhead for multiplexing vs single-stream under 10k long-lived connections
Compatibility tests: run SDK v1 and v2 against canary, ensure v1 receives legacy events and v2 receives resume metadata
Chaos test: simulate replica failover between checkpoint and resume; ensure server can accept resume tokens from previous leader and continue without losing ordering guarantees
dependencies: ENG-23200 - KMS signing endpoint for short-lived tokens
ENG-24110 - SDK v2 streaming client changes (resume logic + idempotency_key generation)
ENG-24401 - Console metric ingestion for resumed_connections and reassembly_errors
comments: 2026-03-09 Asha Patel: Initial ticket created after incidents where mobile clients saw duplicated function calls after reconnect. Proposed opaque token + idempotency approach.

2026-03-10 Devon Li: Spike implemented a prototype encoder using base64-oneline JSON. Observed 8% CPU increase decoding on Node but eliminated edge-case parsing failures seen with multi-line SSE data.
2026-03-11 PM review (Riley Morgan): PMs prefer shorter token TTLs for security; requested dashboard to show percentage of resumed vs fresh connections per customer.
2026-03-12 Design review (Marta Varela): Requested explicit 'stream_reset' and 'stream_snapshot' event types to make migrations deterministic for clients; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-13 QA (Liam O'): Added integration test case where JSON object is split across three events; current reassembly logic handles it but added boundary tests for CRLF variants
